title: debug - e5d1a81c
description:
Looking at the output, the issue is clear: the EMA application is breaking the model's performance. The best validation log loss during training was 0.3335, but after applying EMA, it jumps to 1.1839. The problem is that the code applies EMA to the model before saving (overwriting the best weights) and then applies EMA AGAIN after loading, causing double application of the blurring effect. Additionally, the EMA decay of 0.999 is too aggressive — it barely updates the EMA model, so when applied, the weights are essentially frozen to early training values.

The fix is to:
1. Save the model BEFORE applying EMA, not after
2. Remove the second EMA application after loading
3. Reduce the EMA decay to a more reasonable value (0.995) so it actually tracks recent weights
method: Data preprocessing: loaded train/test CSVs, encoded target labels with LabelEncoder. Feature engineering: extracted 50 handcrafted features including statistical (char/word counts, punctuation, case, digit features), lexical (stopword ratios, unique word ratios, common word ratios), and stylistic (sentence starters, endings, contractions, repeated punctuation) features; also extracted 5000 TF-IDF ngram features. All features were scaled and combined into a sparse matrix. Model architecture: ModernBERT-large (395M parameters) with 3 output classes, label smoothing of 0.1, and dropout rates of 0.3/0.2. Training: used AdamW optimizer with linear warmup scheduler, mixed precision AMP, EMA model averaging, and early stopping with patience of 3. Validation strategy: 5-fold stratified K-fold, using first fold for validation (80/20 split), evaluating with log loss metric.
